question: In otosclerosis, the Carhart notch at 2 kHz on bone-conduction audiometry represents true sensorineural cochlear damage caused by the disease process.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Correct. The Carhart notch at 2 kHz is a mechanical artefact of stapes fixation — it is not true sensorineural damage. It resolves after stapedectomy. Misinterpreting it as irreversible SNHL would incorrectly deny the patient corrective surgery.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Incorrect. The Carhart notch is a mechanical artefact, not true sensorineural damage. It results from reduced ossicular resonance transmitted to the cochlea when the stapes footplate is fixed. It disappears after successful stapedectomy, confirming its mechanical rather than cochlear origin.
